policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 17 Apr close (1x4 3.84, 3x6 3.88, 6x9 3.91, 9x12 3.99 vs WIBOR 3M 3.87) price roughly 10bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC held at 3.75% on 9 Apr; Glapiński sees no near-term change either way - hikes only in a 'black scenario' of renewed war, a question mark over cuts. Wnorowski (17 Apr): rates stable for longer, but signal hike risk if inflation does not stay moderate given loose fiscal policy. March CPI 3.0% (final, 15 Apr; flash 31 Mar, 3.3% expected); core 2.7% (16 Apr). The fuel VAT and excise cuts run to 30 Apr (13 Apr).
policy.risk_text: Two-sided: Hormuz headlines swing oil by up to 10% a day; the MPC holds at least until July (Kotecki), so the front end is anchored near WIBOR while 5-10Y follows Bunds and oil. Supply: April sales of PLN 15-39bn.

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026 (Inflation Report, 6 Mar); the NBP forecaster survey (1 Apr) has 2026 CPI at 2.9%; IMF (14 Apr): 2026 CPI 3.3%. The next projection comes in July.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit 7.2% of GDP (GUS preliminary, 1 Apr), debt 59.7%; 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; S&P (2-6 Apr) sees a 2026 deficit of 7.0% of GDP (8.0% in an oil-shock case); budget deficit after March PLN 69.6bn (25.6% of the limit); fuel package (VAT 8%, minimum excise, price caps) to 30 Apr.
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~41% (end-Q1) financed; USD 6bn of 5Y/10Y/30Y priced on 7 Apr (UST +65/+105/+130bp); budget accounts PLN 169.5bn at end-March. No rating action in April; S&P reviews Poland on 8 May (A-, stable); Fitch A- and Moody's A2 have negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP cut to 3.75% on 4 Mar and held on 9 Apr; March CPI 3.0% y/y; 2025 GDP 3.6%, Q4 revised to 4.1%. Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 17-19 Apr: Wnorowski: rates can stay stable for longer, direction after the July projection; with loose fiscal policy the MPC should signal hike risk if inflation does not stay moderate, and he sees no case for cuts; on 17 Apr the reopening of Hormuz lifted POLGBs, yields -15bp (10Y 5.38%); the fuel package stays for now (energy minister). Abroad: Iran declared Hormuz open on 17 Apr - Brent fell ~10% to below $90, UST and Bund 10Y -8bp (4.23%, 2.96%) and odds of a 2026 Fed cut rose to ~50-60%; on 18 Apr Iran shut the strait again over the US blockade; Tisza confirmed with a two-thirds majority.

calendar.plan_text: MoF April plan (31 Mar): sale auctions on 15 Apr (PLN 4-12bn; OK0128, NZ0331, PS0731, DS1035, NZ0936), 23 Apr (6-14bn) and 28 Apr (5-13bn; new 10Y DS0436 replaces DS1035 from 23 Apr); no switch; a 50-week T-bill on 10 Apr (3-6bn). Q2 plan: 7-8 sales for PLN 50-90bn and 1-2 switches. 2026 needs ~41% financed at end-Q1. 7 Apr: USD 6bn issue (5Y 4.645%, 10Y 5.405%, 30Y 6.233%). 10 Apr T-bill: PLN 3.0bn at 3.95% (demand 3.6bn) plus 0.39bn. 15 Apr sale: PLN 10.71bn vs 12.13bn demand (cover 1.13) plus 0.35bn; PS0731 5.023%, DS1035 5.514%, WS0428 4.271%. BGK FPC (16 Apr): PLN 1.06bn sold on 1.89bn demand plus 0.21bn.
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; March's sell-off broke it. April is back to regular supply: remaining sales 23 Apr, 28 Apr. Next MPC 5-6 May: a hold is expected; the July projection is the next marker. Covers so far: 1.13 (15 Apr) vs 1.17 on 25 Mar.

facts.core_text: Regime: fragile truce with a US blockade of Iranian ports - oil swinging between $90 and $105; the NBP held at 3.75% on 9 Apr while FRAs price roughly 10bp of NBP hikes; the ECB and BoE are priced for hikes, the Fed is on hold, the CNB and MNB are on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 57bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 243bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 17 Apr close). Hormuz opened, then shut; Brent below $90 (17 Apr).

quasi_takeaways: FPC fixed lines trade ~{lo}-{hi}bp over the POLGB curve (average {avg}bp); widest ASW {widest} at {widest_asw}bp. Same State Treasury guarantee as POLGBs.
Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).
Supply: on 16 Apr BGK sold PLN 1.06bn of FPC bonds on 1.89bn demand plus 0.21bn - a first sign of rebuilding demand (PKO); next tender 29 Apr.
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
